newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank says raises main rate to 48.72 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank says raises main rate to 48.72 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) confirmed on Thursday it will raise its main interest rate to 48.72 percent annually from 43.08 percent, to take effect from Monday.
"The BNB board decided to set the main interest rate at... 48.72 percent annually, in force from June 2," the BNB said in a statement. The rise was earlier reported by dealers.
The BNB said the new main rate would give 61.22 percent effective annual interest rate calculated through accumulation of monthly accruals.
The central bank also said the new higher rate was mainly a result of the change in its calculation method.

Last week the BNB said it would adjust the rate only to the weighted average monthly yield on four-week discount T-bills auctioned daily from Friday through Thursday and would not take into account yields on one-week discount paper.
Following that decision the Finance ministry has not issued one-week discount T-bills this week.
Until this week the BNB has adjusted the main rate to the weighted average effective yield on both maturities sold at successive auctions from Friday through Thursday.
Today's rate hike reflected rising yields of short-term government securities at the last five auctions.
Yields to maturity on four-week T-bills auctioned since Friday ranged between 3.76-3.81 percent against 3.55-3.83 percent in the previous five days. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
